In this paper, by use of the subordination principle, we study some geometric

properties of the starlike log–harmonic mappings of order α. Also, we estimate

the Jacobian of log–harmonic mappings.

# 1. Introduction

Let H(∆) be the family of all analytic functions in the open unit disc ∆:=

{z : |z| < 1}. Let f and g be two members of the class H(∆) which satisfy the

normalized conditions f(0) = 0 = f ′(0) − 1 and g(0) = 0 = g′(0) − 1. We say that

a function f is subordinate to g, written f(z) ≺ g(z) or f ≺ g, if there exists an

analytic function ψ, known as a Schwarz function, with ψ(0) = 0 and |ψ(z)| ≤|z|

such that f(z) = g(ψ(z)) for all z ∈ ∆. The set of all univalent (one–to–one)

functions f in ∆is denoted by U. Furthermore, if g ∈U in ∆, then we have the

following equivalence relation

f(z) ≺ g(z) ⇔ f(0) = g(0) and f(∆) ⊂ g(∆).

Also let B(∆) denote the set of all functions w ∈H(∆) satisfying |w(z)| < 1 in ∆.

A mapping f is said to be log–harmonic in ∆, if there exists an analytic function w ∈B(∆) such that f is a solution of the nonlinear elliptic partial diﬀerential

equation
